0|d510d6cc653bc4b3094ea73afe12600d0ab445b3|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: Enable MSI-X for KVM assigned device
This patch finally enable MSI-X.
What we need for MSI-X:
1. Intercept one page in MMIO region of device. So that we can get guest desired
MSI-X table and set up the real one. Now this have been done by guest
transfer to kernel using ioctl KVM_SET_MSIX_NR and KVM_SET_MSIX_ENTRY.
2. Information for incoming interrupt. Now one device can have more than one
interrupt
column2: and they are all handled by one workqueue structure. So we need to

column1: identify them. The previous patch enable gsi_msg_pending_bitmap get this done.
3. Mapping from host IRQ to guest gsi as well as guest gsi to real MSI/MSI-X
message address/data. We used same entry number for the host and guest here
that it's easy to find the correlated guest gsi.
What we lack for now:
1. The PCI spec said nothing can existed with MSI-X table in the same page of
MMIO region
column2: except pending bits. The patch ignore pending bits as the first

column1: step (so they are always 0 - no pending).
2. The PCI spec allowed to change MSI-X table dynamically. That means
can enable MSI-X
didn't support this
column2: and Linux also don't work in this way.

column1: 3. The patch didn't implement MSI-X mask all and mask single entry. I would
implement the former in driver/pci/msi.c later. And for single entry
should have reposibility to handle it.
